title: Reverse Linked List II
statement: Reverse the nodes of the list from position `left` to position `right`, using 1-based positions, and return the value sequence. Do it in one pass.
hints: A dummy node removes the special case where left is 1.
Walk left - 1 steps so you stand on the node before the segment.
Reverse the next (right - left + 1) nodes with the ordinary three-pointer loop, then reconnect both ends.

approaches.name: One-pass pointer reverse
approaches.explanation: Reverse only the requested segment and stitch it back.

editorial: Let prev be the node before position left, and let start be the first node of the segment. Reverse the following right - left nodes by inserting each successor of start directly after prev. That head-insertion formulation keeps start as the tail of the reversed segment, so the final link from start to the remainder is already correct.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def reverse_between(head: list[int], left: int, right: int) -> list[int]:
    dummy = _node_chain([0])
    dummy.nxt = _node_chain(head)
    prev = dummy
    for _ in range(left - 1):
        prev = prev.nxt
    start = prev.nxt
    for _ in range(right - left):
        nxt = start.nxt
        start.nxt = nxt.nxt
        nxt.nxt = prev.nxt
        prev.nxt = nxt
    return _to_list(dummy.nxt)
